title: main.exe silently crashes
body: I tried whisper.net, the compiled Windows x64 binaries from v1.4.0 and v1.2.0, several base models, and the sample jfk.wav. Running `main.exe -m ggml-model-whisper-base.en.bin -f jfk.wav -l en -t 8` prints the model metadata and then the process silently stops. I traced the exit to `whisper_init_from_file` and then `ggml_init`. My system is Windows 10 x64 with an Intel Xeon E5-2640 and a GeForce GTX 1060 6GB. The CPU does not appear to support F16C, and compiling with CUDA support did not change the crash.

symptoms_visible: main.exe prints the model metadata through the model size and then the process silently exits.
The exit occurs while calling whisper_init_from_file, at ggml_init, with every model and Windows binary I tried.
A build with CUDA support exits in the same place.
N0.label: N0 silent model-loading exit reported

symptoms_visible: CMake warns that WHISPER_NO_F16C was not used, and the resulting executable still silently exits at ggml_init.
N1_x.label: N1_x no-F16C option attempt

symptoms_visible: My MSVC build still silently exits at ggml_init, and CMake says the requested instruction-setting variable is unused.
N2.label: N2 MSVC build environment established

symptoms_visible: After pulling the latest master and disabling AVX, AVX2, F16C, and FMA through the available options, the executable still silently exits at ggml_init.
N3_x.label: N3_x latest-master option attempt

symptoms_visible: After rebuilding with the MSVC architecture setting changed from AVX2 to AVX, the model loads and the transcription completes.
The tiny model initially completes in about 164 seconds on this older CPU instead of the process silently exiting.
N_terminal.label: terminal AVX-only MSVC build runs

solution.intent: Rebuild whisper.cpp with the WHISPER_NO_F16C CMake option enabled so the executable does not require F16C.
solution.concrete_example: Create a build directory and run `cmake .. -DWHISPER_NO_F16C=ON`, then rebuild and run the base model.

edges.comment: Issue c3-c6, reporter's Windows system: participant1 suggested WHISPER_NO_F16C, but the reporter's CMake run warned that the variable was not used and the executable continued to exit.

question_patterns: Which compiler and generator are you using for the Windows build?
Are you building with MSVC, MinGW, or another compiler?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I'm compiling with MSVC. CMake warns that WHISPER_NO_F16C is a manually specified variable that the project does not use.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I'm building with GCC on Linux, and the compile command contains only the instruction flags I explicitly enabled.
I'm using a different Visual Studio release, but it is still an MSVC-generated build with the same unused-variable warning.

edges.comment: Issue c4-c6, reporter's system: the reporter disclosed that the failing build used MSVC and that CMake did not recognize the proposed variable.

solution.intent: Pull the latest master, where the instruction-disabling options should work, and rebuild with AVX2, F16C, FMA, and other unsupported instruction paths disabled.
solution.concrete_example: Update to the latest master, configure a fresh build with the available AVX, AVX2, F16C, and FMA options disabled, and rerun the sample.

edges.comment: Issue c7-c8, reporter's system: participant1 suggested pulling latest master; the reporter rebuilt while disabling AVX, AVX2, F16C, and FMA, but the executable still exited.

solution.intent: Correct the MSVC-specific build configuration that unconditionally requests AVX2: change the compiler architecture argument from `/arch:avx2` to `/arch:avx`, rebuild, and have the reporter verify that model loading and transcription complete.
solution.concrete_example: In the MSVC branch of CMakeLists.txt, replace the unconditional `/arch:avx2` compiler argument with `/arch:avx`, regenerate a clean build, and run the JFK sample again.
solution.inference_hint: Participant2 inspected the MSVC-specific CMake branch and determined that it passed `/arch:avx2` regardless of the nominal instruction options. The reporter supplied the compiler, CPU, warnings, and repeated crash results; connecting those facts to the unconditional MSVC argument is engineer-side inference.

edges.comment: Issue c9-c13, reporter's system: participant2 identified the unconditional MSVC `/arch:avx2` argument and advised changing it to `/arch:avx`. The reporter rebuilt, confirmed that the model ran and completed, and later reported acceptable performance with suitable AVX-only build settings, BLAS, and multiple threads.

solution.intent: For a Windows MSVC build on the older Xeon, inspect the compiler architecture argument rather than relying on the CMake feature toggles; replace an unconditional `/arch:avx2` with `/arch:avx`, rebuild, and verify the sample completes.
solution.concrete_example: Check the MSVC section of CMakeLists.txt. If it always adds `/arch:avx2`, change that argument to `/arch:avx`, make a clean rebuild, and rerun `main.exe` with jfk.wav.
solution.inference_hint: This shortcut represents proposing the accepted source-level MSVC architecture correction immediately from the Windows and CPU evidence. The real thread only established the unconditional `/arch:avx2` behavior after the no-F16C and latest-master attempts failed.

edges.comment: Shortcut copy of the accepted c9-c10 solution so a correct first response can match without forcing the reporter through the two failed rebuild attempts.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: the MSVC-specific build configuration unconditionally passed `/arch:avx2`, so changing CMake feature options did not prevent an AVX2-targeted executable from being built for the older Xeon.
Must ground the diagnosis in the Windows Xeon E5-2640 setup, the MSVC build, the unused CMake option warning, and the continued exit after nominally disabling instruction features.
Must recommend changing the MSVC compiler architecture argument from `/arch:avx2` to `/arch:avx` and rebuilding the executable.
Must not present CUDA support or the WHISPER_NO_F16C and related CMake toggles alone as the fix; those approaches were tried without stopping the exit under MSVC.
Must ask the reporter to verify that a rebuilt binary loads the model and completes transcription before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Moderately technical Windows user who can compile C++ projects, edit build files, test compiler options, and trace a native crash to a function, but needs guidance on CMake and MSVC-specific behavior.
persona_hint.communication_style: Polite, persistent, and iterative; reports exact commands and observations, updates hypotheses openly, and expresses appreciation when advice works.
